claims.text: The three artifacts describe the same trip, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip identifier TRP-02819 and the trace runs from the recorded trip-start at 16:25:31 to trip-completion at 16:32:51. The trace is also unimpaired for policy purposes - 100.0% coverage, 45 fixes at a 10-second sample interval, zero gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds - so no consequence under POL-RD-07(a) to (c) arises and the distance it measures stands as the measured distance for this trip.

On the governing trace figure of 3.96 km against the booked optimal of 3.2 km, the excess is 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of the optimal route and therefore above POL-RD-01's 20% percentage limb. POL-RD-01 requires this measurement to be taken from gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not from the rounded 4.0 km convenience copy on the trip record, and the rider cites the trace figure. I do not put the percentage limb forward as establishing the deviation on its own, because the clause requires both limbs to pass and the rider addresses the second limb squarely in a separate claim below.

The driver's only explanation on file is 'One-way streets'. That is an external traffic cause asserted with no evidence ID, and there is no traffic_advisory in this bundle: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code that fired is MISSING_ARTIFACT (severity BLOCKING). Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08, which discards assertions that cite no evidence ID. I disclose the impairment of the artifact I rely on: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is cited for its absence alone, which POL-GEN-02(3) makes citable. The driver's account also has no artifact behind it at all - the chat log for this trip carries zero messages from either party.

No clause on this record supplies the driver with an amended optimal or with any reduction of the measured excess. The chat log carries zero messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction route is unavailable and its 200 m corroboration test cannot be run on the record; both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so POL-RD-05 has no amendment to re-quote and must not be given a substitute figure; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's pooled-itinerary baseline does not apply and the 3.2 km booked optimal stands untouched.

The fare model on this trip is METERED and the trip record carries no quoted_fare_sgd, so POL-RD-11's bar on distance-and-time refunds for upfront-quoted trips does not apply here, and POL-RD-02's arithmetic is the operative remedy rather than the pass-through correction alone. The surge multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, which records 1.0, as POL-RD-02 requires; the trip record does not carry that field at all and no higher multiplier may be assumed.

If the tribunal finds the deviation established, the POL-RD-02 computation is ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 8.68, against a charged total of 9.64; the refund is 0.96, which is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of the charged total, so the outcome would be PARTIAL_REFUND, rounded up to SGD 1.00. The rider asks for that figure only if establishment is found on the trace.

The rider's 60-day profile does not engage POL-RD-08's additional corroboration requirement. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, below the clause's trigger of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated, so the excess the rider has shown is to be decided on this trip's trace evidence and no corroboration beyond the trace may be demanded of this claim.

I concede the point the record will not carry. On the governing trace figure the excess is 0.76 km, which is not greater than 0.8 km, and POL-RD-01 requires both the percentage and the absolute limb to pass; the rider therefore does not ask the tribunal to find the deviation established and does not ask it to read the threshold any other way. The two distance fields on this record straddle that threshold by 40 metres - 0.76 km on the trace, 0.80 km on the rounded copy - and the policy resolves the straddle against the rider by making the trace figure govern, so the shortfall is the rider's and the rider says so.

The governing distance measurement is the trace, not the trip record, and on the trace no deviation is established. EV-GPS-02819 records trace_distance_km of 3.96 km; EV-TRIP-02819 stores the booked optimal_distance_km as 3.2 km. The excess is therefore 0.76 km, which the platform's own derived block states as excess_km 0.76 / excess_pct 23.75 and tags status 'no deviation'. POL-RD-01 is a two-limb gate: a deviation is ESTABLISHED only when the excess is greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms, and both tests must pass. The percentage limb is cleared at 23.75%, but the absolute limb fails by 0.04 km. No deviation exists, and under POL-RD-01 the outcome is NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip.

The threshold test fails even on the reading most favourable to the rider. POL-RD-01 fixes which field governs where the two distance fields disagree: gps_trace.trace_distance_km governs, and trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy that may NOT be cited for the threshold test. EV-TRIP-02819 rounds the same measurement up to 4.0 km, and 4.0 km less the 3.2 km optimal is exactly 0.80 km — not greater than 0.80 km. The absolute limb therefore fails on the rounded figure as well, so the result is the same whichever field is read.

The 3.2 km comparator is not displaced by any adjustment clause, so the threshold arithmetic above stands as measured. EV-TRIP-02819 carries pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at as null and amended_optimal_distance_km as null, so there is no re-quote and POL-RD-05 cannot run; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply and solo_optimal_distance_km is not in issue. The booked optimal of 3.2 km is the correct baseline for POL-RD-01.

The trace is unimpaired, so the measured figure can be relied on and no gap-handling consequences arise. EV-GPS-02819 carries 45 fixes at a 10 second sample interval against a 10 second expected interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps and max_gap_sec 0.0. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 — a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained interval above 30 seconds — is met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and the POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is not engaged. The deviation finding, such as it is, rests on a clean trace.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. The rider must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. No artifact in this bundle shows an excess above 0.8 km; the highest figure available anywhere is the 0.76 km on EV-GPS-02819, and the rounded copy on EV-TRIP-02819 yields at most 0.80 km, which does not exceed the threshold. The burden never shifts to the driver, and there is nothing for the driver to excuse.

For completeness on the driver's side, the asserted traffic cause does not exonerate anything, and I do not ask the tribunal to treat it as if it did. The driver's statement is 'One-way streets'. The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this corridor: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own note records that no advisory covers the Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres corridor in this window. That impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run — there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses and no validity window to compare — and under POL-RD-13 the uncited traffic assertion carries no weight and neither reduces nor supplies an amended optimal. That costs the driver nothing, because the excess never reaches the POL-RD-01 threshold in the first place.

The absent advisory does not turn this into an escalation. Under POL-RD-13(1), where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The driver's statement cites no advisory identifier, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire on account of the traffic explanation.

Nothing in the fare ledger supports a standalone correction of any kind. EV-FARE-02819 shows erp_lines totalling 0.00 with no gantries, tolls_erp 0.0, airport_surcharge 0.0, waiting_time_fee 0.0, promo_discount 0.0 and surge_multiplier 1.0; the trip does not originate at an airport and the trace crosses no gantry. There is no off-route ERP to pass through, no surcharge wrongly applied, and therefore no billing-integrity finding or referral under POL-RD-09(4).

Two of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers are affirmatively excluded on this record. First, POL-RD-10(2): the trip identifier is TRP-02819 on all three deciding artifacts, EV-TRIP-02819, EV-GPS-02819 and EV-FARE-02819, so the identifiers match and the trip record is present. Second, POL-RD-10(4): the trace's first and last fixes, 2026-08-28T16:25:31 and 2026-08-28T16:32:51, coincide exactly with the recorded start and end timestamps on the trip record, and no admitted artifact's timestamps run backwards. Nothing here requires a human reviewer.

The remaining POL-RD-10 escalation triggers are also excluded. POL-RD-10(8): every charge line on EV-FARE-02819 — base fare 3.80, distance charge for 4.0 billed km, time charge for 7.3 min and the 0.80 platform fee — has a counterpart in EV-TRIP-02819's recorded distance and duration and in the trace, so there is no charge line without a counterpart. POL-RD-10(7): EV-CHAT-02819 contains zero messages, so there is no chat detour request and no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength. POL-RD-10(6): no refund is in issue at all, let alone one above SGD 150.00 or above charged_total.

Even if the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern is established and none of the clause's three effects can follow. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 on EV-DPROF-02819, below the 3 the clause requires, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 314 is 0.32%, far below the 5% limb, with the 314 trips comfortably above the clause's 40-trip minimum. There is accordingly no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two 90-day fields; driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the field POL-RD-06 names.

NO_ACTION is the right outcome and on a rider-filed dispute it is a win for the driver. The dispute was filed by the RIDER, and EV-FARE-02819 records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and total_charged 9.64. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present payment state stands — the fare already collected is left with the platform and no amount moves — so the driver keeps the metered fare and the rider's contested SGD 1.50 is not returned.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the deviation gate fails and the fare already charged stands. The governing distance is the GPS trace, EV-GPS-02819, which measures 3.96 km; the booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-02819 is 3.2 km. The excess is therefore 0.76 km, or 23.75% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 requires BOTH limbs to pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of the optimal distance AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The percentage limb passes (23.75% > 20%), but the absolute limb fails (0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km). The trace figure governs and the trip record's rounded 4.0 km may not be used for the threshold test; even that figure gives exactly 0.80 km, which likewise is not greater than 0.80 km. No deviation is established, and POL-RD-01 directs the outcome NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip. The SGD 9.64 charged on EV-FARE-02819 stands and the SGD 1.50 the rider contests is not returned. This is not a win for either side on the merits of the route; it is the threshold doing its job.

No adjustment clause displaces the 3.2 km baseline. The trip record carries no amendment (pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null), so POL-RD-05 cannot run. The vehicle is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12's matched-itinerary baseline does not apply. The chat log EV-CHAT-02819 carries zero messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction route is unavailable and its 200 m test cannot be run.

The driver's explanation 'One-way streets' is an external-traffic assertion with no traffic_advisory behind it. EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. Under POL-RD-13 and POL-RD-08 that assertion carries no weight and exonerates nothing. It does not need to: the excess never reaches the threshold, so nothing turns on it, and no escalation follows from the missing advisory because no party cited the absent identifier.

Nothing else is refundable. EV-FARE-02819 shows ERP of 0.00 with no gantries, no airport surcharge, no waiting-time fee and no promo discount, so there is no billing-integrity defect and no POL-RD-09(4) referral. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07 and POL-RD-10(3) are not engaged. All three deciding artifacts carry trip TRP-02819 with consistent timestamps, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) are excluded. The driver profile, EV-DPROF-02819, shows 1 deviation flag in 90 days against 314 completed trips — far below the POL-RD-06 pattern test — so there is no conduct referral and no FULL_REFUND uplift. The rider's own POL-RD-02 arithmetic (recomputed fare 8.68 against a charged total of 9.64, a refund of 0.96 rounded up to SGD 1.00) is not reached, because that computation only runs once a deviation is established. Confidence is 0.90, capped by the weight-1.0 artifacts (EV-GPS-02819 and EV-TRIP-02819) that carry the deciding measurement. The monetary effect is nil, below the automatic execution threshold, so no amount moves.

ruling.explanation: Both parties agree, and the record confirms, that no route deviation is established on this trip. POL-RD-01 makes gps_trace.trace_distance_km the governing measurement (3.96 km on EV-GPS-02819) over the rounded convenience copy on the trip record (4.0 km), and sets a two-limb gate: the excess must be both more than 20% of the optimal route and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms. Against the booked optimal of 3.2 km (EV-TRIP-02819) the excess is 0.76 km — 23.75%, so the percentage limb passes — but 0.76 km is not greater than 0.8 km, so the absolute limb fails. Even on the rounded 4.0 km figure the excess is exactly 0.80 km, which still does not exceed the threshold. Because one limb fails, POL-RD-01 fixes the outcome at NO_ACTION however the rider characterises the trip, unless a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4) is available; none is, because EV-FARE-02819 shows erp_lines totalling 0.00, no tolls and airport_surcharge 0.0, and the trip crosses no gantry. POL-RD-02 is therefore not reached: had a deviation been established the arithmetic would have been ((3.80 + 0.75 x 3.2 + 0.28 x 6.0) x 1.0, the multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier) + 0.80 = 8.68 against charged_total 9.64, a refund of 0.96 rounded up to SGD 1.00 — but that finding does not exist. The rider's own concession to that effect is accepted; the rider's point that the percentage limb is cleared is correct but insufficient, since both limbs must pass. The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 — 45 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100.0% coverage, zero gaps, max gap 0.0 s — so limbs (a) to (c) are not met and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. No adjustment clause supplies an amended optimal: pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null (POL-RD-05 unavailable), EV-CHAT-02819 carries zero messages (POL-RD-04 unavailable), and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL (POL-RD-12 inapplicable), so the booked 3.2 km stands. The driver's 'One-way streets' explanation carries no weight: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, weight_multiplier 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so there is no traffic_advisory against which to test it; under POL-RD-13 an uncited traffic assertion neither exonerates excess nor supplies an amended optimal. Because the driver named no advisory identifier, the missing advisory is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, and it is not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation. No other POL-RD-10 trigger fires: the trip identifiers all match on TRP-02819, the trace's first and last fixes coincide with the recorded trip start and end, every charge line has a counterpart in the trip record and trace, and no refund above SGD 150.00 is in issue. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check establishes no repeat-deviation pattern — deviation_flags_90d is 1, below the 3 required, and 1 over 314 completed trips is far below the 5% limb — so there is neither a FULL_REFUND uplift nor a POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral; driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and, as POL-GEN-01 provides, is not the trailing-90-day field that test names. POL-RD-08's additional corroboration requirement is not engaged: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, below the trigger of 4 or more claims with 1 or fewer substantiated. Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION on a rider-filed dispute means the rider's claim is not supported by the evidence and the present payment state stands: EV-FARE-02819 records payment_status CHARGED, total_charged 9.64 and refund_issued_sgd 0.00, and no amount moves. The monetary effect is nil and so below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold; this ruling is provisional and either party may appeal under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver. The whole case turns on 40 metres, and the policy resolves it.

DISTANCE. The distance actually driven is the GPS trace on EV-GPS-02819: 3.96 km. The booked optimal route on EV-TRIP-02819 is 3.2 km. The excess is therefore 0.76 km, which is 23.75% of the optimal route. POL-RD-01 makes that a deviation only if BOTH limbs of its gate pass: the excess must be greater than 20% of the optimal route (it is, at 23.75%) AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms (it is not — 0.76 km falls 40 m short). One limb fails, so no deviation is established for this trip. The trip record's rounded 4.0 km would give exactly 0.80 km, which also does not exceed 0.80 km, and POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure govern the threshold test in any case, so the result is the same whichever field is read. The rider's advocate conceded this point, correctly.

WHAT FOLLOWS. Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-01 sends the case to NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised, and the only route left open by that clause is a billing-integrity refund under POL-RD-09(4), which does not arise here. The rider's alternative arithmetic — charged_total 9.64 less a recomputed_fare of 8.68, a refund of 0.96 rounded up to 1.00 — is therefore moot: POL-RD-02 never runs. The SGD 1.50 the rider contested is not refunded, the metered fare of 9.64 stands, and refund_issued_sgd remains 0.00.

THE DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. 'One-way streets' is an assertion of an external traffic cause citing no evidence. There is no traffic advisory for this corridor anywhere in the bundle: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, its weight_multiplier is 0.0 and the issue code that fired is MISSING_ARTIFACT. POL-RD-03 cannot be run without an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window, so the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08 and POL-RD-13 and neither reduces nor replaces the measured excess. It does not escalate the case either: the driver named no advisory identifier, and POL-RD-13(1) provides that an assertion citing no artifact cannot invoke POL-RD-10(5) against one. The chat log (EV-CHAT-02819) holds zero messages, so POL-RD-04's rider-instruction route is unavailable and its 200 m test could not be run, and POL-RD-05's amendment route is closed (pickup, dropoff and amended optimal are all null).

THE MONEY LINES. EV-FARE-02819 shows ERP and tolls of 0.00 with no gantry charged, an airport surcharge of 0.00 on a trip that does not originate at an airport, a zero waiting-time fee and a zero promo discount: no phantom line, and no billing-integrity referral under POL-RD-09(4). The fare model is METERED with no quoted fare, so POL-RD-11's upfront-quote bar is not in issue, and the surge multiplier read from EV-FARE-02819 is 1.0. Every charge line has a counterpart in the trip record's distance and duration, so POL-RD-10(8) is not engaged.

REMAINING CLAIMS. The POL-RD-06 driver-profile check shows no repeat deviation pattern (deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 314, which is 0.32%, with 314 trips above the 40-trip minimum), so there is no FULL_REFUND uplift and no driver-conduct referral; the check was confined to the two 90-day fields POL-GEN-01 permits, and the lifetime prior_deviation_flags counter was not used. The rider's 60-day profile does not trigger POL-RD-08's corroboration requirement (1 claim, 0 substantiated). The trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (45 fixes, 10-second interval, 100% coverage, zero gaps, no jump over 500 m), so no gap-handling consequence and no POL-RD-10(3) escalation arises. Trip identifiers and timestamps match across EV-TRIP-02819, EV-GPS-02819 and EV-FARE-02819, so POL-RD-10(2) and (4) are excluded, and no other POL-RD-10 trigger fires. The vehicle is RYDE_X, so POL-RD-12's pooled-itinerary baseline does not apply and the 3.2 km booked optimal stands; and there is no unbilled-distance shortfall, so no POL-RD-04 driver compensation is due.

CONFIDENCE AND PROCESS. Confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor; the ruling rests on EV-GPS-02819 and EV-TRIP-02819, both at full weight 1.0, and on no impaired artifact. The monetary effect is nil, well below the automatic-execution threshold. One driver submission was discarded by the citation check for citing the impaired advisory without naming its issue code; the rider's submissions on the same advisory did disclose its weight of 0.0 and MISSING_ARTIFACT and were considered.

THE GATE. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km absolute. The percentage limb passes (23.75%). The absolute limb fails: 0.76 km is not greater than 0.80 km. Because both limbs must pass, no deviation exists on this trip and the outcome is NO_ACTION however the trip is characterised. The rider advocate's concession to precisely this effect is accepted, and the rider is right that the two distance fields straddle the threshold — the policy resolves that straddle against the rule the rider seeks. The driver advocate's threshold claims are accepted for the same reason: even on the rounded 4.00 km copy the excess is exactly 0.80 km, which still does not exceed 0.80 km, so the result is identical whichever field is read.

POL-RD-02 does not run: there is no established deviation against which to recompute the fare, so the recomputed figure of 8.68 and the 0.96 difference against the charged total of 9.64 are not reached and are not paid. The contest is therefore not the rider's SGD 1.50 in the sense claimed. No exculpatory adjustment is needed on either side: POL-RD-04 supplies nothing because EV-CHAT-02819 carries zero messages and its 200 m corroboration test cannot be run; POL-RD-05 supplies nothing because pickup_amended_at, dropoff_amended_at and amended_optimal_distance_km are all null and no substitute re-quote may be invented; POL-RD-12 does not apply because the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. TRACE INTEGRITY. The POL-RD-10(3) escalation route is therefore not engaged and no independent corroboration is demanded.

For completeness, the bundle holds no traffic advisory for this corridor — EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and, under POL-RD-13, an assertion of an external traffic cause that cites no advisory identifier is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation, and it neither reduces the excess nor supplies an amended optimal.

The rider must show, citing evidence IDs, an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. No artifact in this bundle shows an excess above 0.8 km; the highest figure available anywhere is the 0.76 km on EV-GPS-02819, and the rounded copy on EV-TRIP-02819 yields at most 0.80 km, which does not exceed the threshold. The burden never shifts to the driver, and there is nothing for the driver to excuse.

For completeness on the driver's side, the asserted traffic cause does not exonerate anything, and I do not ask the tribunal to treat it as if it did. The driver's statement is 'One-way streets'. The bundle holds no traffic advisory for this corridor: EV-ADVIS-02819-01 is MISSING, carries weight_multiplier 0.0 and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its own note records that no advisory covers the Blk 12 Telok Blangah Cres corridor in this window. That impairment is disclosed here as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. POL-RD-03 therefore cannot be run — there is no advisory naming a road the optimal route traverses and no validity window to compare — and under POL-RD-13 the uncited traffic assertion carries no weight and neither reduces nor supplies an amended optimal. That costs the driver nothing, because the excess never reaches the POL-RD-01 threshold in the first place.

The absent advisory does not turn this into an escalation. Under POL-RD-13(1), where the asserting party names no evidence ID for an advisory, the missing advisory is not an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact within POL-RD-10(5): an assertion that cites no artifact cannot be invoked against one, and the absence of an artifact no party has cited is a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction in it. The driver's statement cites no advisory identifier, so POL-RD-10(5) does not fire on account of the traffic explanation.
ledger.detail: the claim cites impaired artifact EV-ADVIS-02819-01 at weight_multiplier 0.0 but does not name its issue code(s): MISSING_ARTIFACT

ledger.claim: Nothing in the fare ledger supports a standalone correction of any kind. EV-FARE-02819 shows erp_lines totalling 0.00 with no gantries, tolls_erp 0.0, airport_surcharge 0.0, waiting_time_fee 0.0, promo_discount 0.0 and surge_multiplier 1.0; the trip does not originate at an airport and the trace crosses no gantry. There is no off-route ERP to pass through, no surcharge wrongly applied, and therefore no billing-integrity finding or referral under POL-RD-09(4).

Two of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers are affirmatively excluded on this record. First, POL-RD-10(2): the trip identifier is TRP-02819 on all three deciding artifacts, EV-TRIP-02819, EV-GPS-02819 and EV-FARE-02819, so the identifiers match and the trip record is present. Second, POL-RD-10(4): the trace's first and last fixes, 2026-08-28T16:25:31 and 2026-08-28T16:32:51, coincide exactly with the recorded start and end timestamps on the trip record, and no admitted artifact's timestamps run backwards. Nothing here requires a human reviewer.

The remaining POL-RD-10 escalation triggers are also excluded. POL-RD-10(8): every charge line on EV-FARE-02819 — base fare 3.80, distance charge for 4.0 billed km, time charge for 7.3 min and the 0.80 platform fee — has a counterpart in EV-TRIP-02819's recorded distance and duration and in the trace, so there is no charge line without a counterpart. POL-RD-10(7): EV-CHAT-02819 contains zero messages, so there is no chat detour request and no mutually contradictory evidence of comparable strength. POL-RD-10(6): no refund is in issue at all, let alone one above SGD 150.00 or above charged_total.

Even if the POL-RD-06 driver-profile check were consulted, no repeat-deviation pattern is established and none of the clause's three effects can follow. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 on EV-DPROF-02819, below the 3 the clause requires, and 1 divided by completed_trips_90d of 314 is 0.32%, far below the 5% limb, with the 314 trips comfortably above the clause's 40-trip minimum. There is accordingly no FULL_REFUND uplift and no POL-RD-06(c) conduct referral. POL-GEN-01 confines this test to those two 90-day fields; driver_profile.prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter and is not the field POL-RD-06 names.
flags: context-only profile field mentioned in claim text: prior_deviation_flags

ledger.claim: NO_ACTION is the right outcome and on a rider-filed dispute it is a win for the driver. The dispute was filed by the RIDER, and EV-FARE-02819 records payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 and total_charged 9.64. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION ruling means the filing party's claim is not supported and the present payment state stands — the fare already collected is left with the platform and no amount moves — so the driver keeps the metered fare and the rider's contested SGD 1.50 is not returned.
